headline: HONEY BADGER SILVER DRILLS 1,535 G/T AGEQ IN NWT — First 2026 Holes Hit 4.38m of Extreme Grade at Sunrise Lake; Second Hole Adds 17m at 537 G/T
snippet: Honey Badger Silver (TSXV: TUF) released first 2026 drill results from the Sunrise Lake Project, Northwest Territories on November 25, with the headline hole SR-26-004 returning 18.22 metres at 434 g/t silver equivalent including 4.38 metres at 1,535 g/t, and SR-26-001 returning 17 metres at 537 g/t including 7.30 metres at 1,154 g/t. Historical drilling at Sunrise Lake reached 750 metres depth — well beyond the 500-metre historical resource boundary — suggesting the mineralised system has significant upside beyond the existing estimate, the kind of open-at-depth characteristic that drives multi-phase drill programs.

headline: DEVELOP GLOBAL PARKS PIONEER DOME — Spodumene -50% Since September Forces December 31 Care-and-Maintenance
snippet: Develop Global (ASX: DVP) announced on November 25 it will suspend Pioneer Dome lithium operations on December 31, citing a 50% collapse in spodumene prices since September 2026, with CEO Bill Beament stating production 'cannot be justified at current market prices.' The suspension comes weeks after the mine's first lithium shipment under its Trafigura floor-price DSO agreement; the company retains a small site crew for rapid restart and continues studying Stage 2 underground economics, but the broader signal is clear: at current lithium prices, even recently commissioned Australian hard-rock mines cannot operate profitably.

headline: SILVER OUTPERFORMS GOLD ON THANKSGIVING — Spot Rises 1.39% to $41.69 as Gold/Silver Ratio Drops to 85.73
snippet: Spot silver rallied 1.39% to $41.69 per troy ounce on November 26, reclaiming territory lost when it crashed below $40 for the first time in months on Wednesday's hotter-than-expected US PCE data; the gold-silver ratio fell to 85.73 from 86.93, suggesting silver is beginning to lead the bounce. For mining investors, silver's relative strength in a precious metals recovery is historically a leading indicator of junior miner performance, since silver explorers carry higher operating leverage to price than their gold peers and typically re-rate first in a commodity cycle reversal.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD: 110.47 G/T FROM SURFACE AT ICEBERG — K2 Infill Confirms Mine Plan at Queensway; Q4 2027 Production on Track
snippet: New Found Gold (TSX: NFGC) released Iceberg and K2 grade-control results on November 24, with the headline Iceberg intercept returning 110.47 g/t gold over 2.60 metres from just 27.55 metres depth, plus 14.58 g/t over 12 metres from 1.65 metres — confirming at-surface high grade across a 10,071-metre, 88-hole program at Queensway, Newfoundland. K2 infill drilling confirmed continuity of mineralisation that supports the mine plan, with Phase 1 mining targeted for Q4 2027; near-surface 110 g/t at a construction-stage project is the grade profile that justifies the capital required to bring a mine into production.

headline: NEXGEN PCE URANIUM FOOTPRINT UP 29% DEEPER — High-Grade Core Now 739m; 2026 Program Three-Quarters Complete
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX/NYSE: NXE) reported that its 2026 drilling campaign at Patterson Corridor East (PCE) has grown the overall mineralized footprint 29% vertically to 905 metres and along strike to 678 metres, with the high-grade subdomain now extending 739 metres deep across 15 additional holes — 31,480 of a planned 42,000 metres complete. PCE sits 3.5 km from NexGen's fully permitted Arrow Deposit in the Athabasca Basin; continued zone expansion at this proximity reinforces the argument that the Arrow Basin hosts a second major uranium accumulation that could reach Arrow-scale economics.

headline: ABU DHABI'S IRH TABLES $464M CASH BID FOR KENMARE RESOURCES — 52% Premium, Dec 15 Deadline; Mozambique Approval Required
snippet: International Resources Holding (IRH), an Abu Dhabi state-linked resource group, agreed pre-conditional terms on November 24 to pay 380p per share in cash for Irish mineral-sands producer Kenmare Resources (LSE: KMR), valuing it at approximately £487 million including debt — a 52% premium to its last close — with Kenmare's board unanimously minded to recommend. The deal requires Mozambique government approval for a change of control at the Moma titanium-ilmenite mine, and IRH has until December 15 to firm up or walk away under Irish takeover rules; the offer comes as Kenmare's weak mineral-sands prices have pressured cash flow, making a sovereign-linked buyer with patient capital the natural acquirer.

headline: METALSOURCE SILVER HILL STEP-OUT: 103 G/T AGEQ OVER 17.28M — High-Grade Polymetallic Corridor Extends South in BC
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) reported a corrected step-out intercept on November 24 at Silver Hill, BC — hole SH26-27 returned 17.28 metres at 103 g/t silver equivalent including a 0.67-metre peak of 1,192 g/t AgEq, with an earlier uncorrected release having understated the grade — confirming the high-grade polymetallic corridor extends at least 33 metres south of previously identified mineralisation. The consistent near-surface geometry at high grades positions the Silver Hill corridor for rapid resource growth through additional step-out drilling.

headline: SPROTT: WESTERN RARE EARTH SUPPLY SHOULD BE "UNASSAILABLE" — China Export Controls Have Built the Political Will That Exploration Lacked
snippet: A Sprott Asset Management analysis published November 26 argues that China's escalating export controls — which have driven yttrium oxide to $1,650/kg in North America versus roughly $9/kg inside China — have created the political will and economic incentive to build an ex-China rare earth supply chain that should be treated as strategically unassailable by institutional capital. Western REE explorers and developers, whose valuations have compressed dramatically even as the strategic argument for their assets has never been stronger, stand to benefit as governments from France to Japan accelerate critical mineral reserve-building programs.

headline: BERNSTEIN: OVERWEIGHT GOLD AND IRON ORE, AVOID COPPER — Names Rio Tinto Top Pick at Current Sector Lows
snippet: Bernstein's November 23 metals and mining research report reaffirmed Rio Tinto as top pick with an $86.50 US target, recommended overweight exposure to gold and iron ore as defensive positions amid market volatility, and explicitly cautioned against heavy copper allocations — noting sector valuations have fallen below their historical discount range but that broad bottom-fishing remains premature. For retail investors navigating November's commodity sell-off, Bernstein's framework offers an institutional-grade positioning map: gold and iron ore as stabilisers while copper's AI-demand reset plays out, with copper equities becoming 'increasingly more interesting' at current levels but not yet a buy signal.
